menu.reconcile_note: The single on-target artifact is the sole caller fcn.00417cfc (0x417cfc), the firmware-upgrade routine (only jal to the gate is at 0x41828c). It shows this function's return is the authorization for a flash write: when the gate returns non-zero the caller returns 0xffffffff and performs no write, and only when the gate returns 0 does it fall through to write the uploaded image to /dev/mtdblock5 via func_0x00417b9c (fopen + fwrite). The ORIGINAL returns 0xffffffff (deny) on the signature-mismatch else branch, so the caller aborts and no unauthenticated image is flashed: not-vulnerable. The same caller context does not neutralize the mutant: M4 returns 0 (allow) on that same mismatch branch, so the caller does not abort and flashes an image whose signature does not match the device. The menu resolves the return-consumption question that makes the gate body need-more-context on its own; the deciding flaw lives in the mutant's own body, so under the identical menu the mutant stays vulnerable.
